\## 1. This week's analysis


```{bash}
#opening qiime2, giving it the manifest and how to read the manifest (input-format) so it knows where my data lives. Using a qiime2 tool and putting the output from into week 3 output folder for this workflow. 

source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/week3/03.2-metabarcoding-workflow

qiime tools import \
  --type 'SampleData[PairedEndSequencesWithQuality]' \
  --input-path ~/Dailey-546/data/manifest.tsv \
  --input-format PairedEndFastqManifestPhred33V2 \
  --output-path demux.qza
```

```{bash}
#visualizing read counts per sample in qiime
#nothing trimmed or changed yet

source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/week3/03.2-metabarcoding-workflow

qiime demux summarize \

```

Primers are S-D-Bact-0341-b-S-17/S-D-Bact-0785-a-A-21.

```{bash}
#trimming
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/week3/03.2-metabarcoding-workflow

qiime cutadapt trim-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-sequences demux.qza \
  --p-front-f "CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG" \
  --p-front-r "GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC" \
  --p-discard-untrimmed \
  --p-cores 8 \
  --o-trimmed-sequences 16s-demux.qza \
  --o-stats 16s-cutadapt-stats.qza
```

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/week3/03.2-metabarcoding-workflow

qiime dada2 denoise-paired \
  --i-demultiplexed-seqs 16s-demux.qza \
  --p-trunc-len-f 270 \
  --p-trunc-len-r 200 \
  --p-n-threads 16 \
  --o-table 16s-table.qza \
  --o-representative-sequences 16s-rep-seqs.qza \
  --o-denoising-stats 16s-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-base-transition-stats 16s-dada2-error-model.qza
```

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../output/week3/03.2-metabarcoding-workflow

qiime metadata tabulate \
  --m-input-file 16s-dada2-stats.qza \
  --o-visualization 16s-dada2-stats.qzv
```

```{bash}
#downloading SILVA database, which is the reference database that is often best for 16s data. This is not classifier trained for my specific primers, so it won't be specific to the V3-V4 region I targeted
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ../data/reference

if [ ! -f silva-138.2-seqs.qza ] || [ ! -f silva-138.2-taxonomy.qza ]; then
  qiime rescript get-silva-data \
    --p-version '138.2' \
    --p-target 'SSURef_NR99' \
    --o-silva-sequences silva-138.2-seqs.qza \
    --o-silva-taxonomy silva-138.2-taxonomy.qza
fi

```

```{bash}
source /opt/anaconda/anaconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate qiime2-2026.7
cd ~/Dailey-546/data/reference

# Convert reference RNA sequences to DNA
qiime rescript reverse-transcribe \
  --i-rna-sequences silva-138.2-seqs.qza \
  --o-dna-sequences silva-138.2-dna-seqs.qza
  
qiime feature-classifier extract-reads \
  --i-sequences silva-138.2-dna-seqs.qza \
  --p-f-primer CCTACGGGNGGCWGCAG \
  --p-r-primer GACTACHVGGGTATCTAATCC \
  --o-reads silva-138.2-klind-seqs.qza \
  --o-read-extraction-stats silva-138.2-klind-extraction-stats.qza
```


\## 2. Reflection questions

1.  What is the difference between mapping reads to a reference and assembling reads without one?

Assembling reads without a reference (de novo assembly) reconstructs longer DNA sequences by identifying overlaps among shorter reads and joining them together without any reference genome. Mapping aligns reads to an existing reference genome to determine where they likely originated.

2.  What intermediate summary would you inspect before trusting a mapping or quantification result? It is important to check the number of input reads, number or proportion mapped, the output file size and format, check out asmall preview of the result, and also look at logs or summary reports.

3.  What is the smallest meaningful workflow slice you can run for your project this week?

I think the smallest workflow slice would be to get my project reads to a place where they are ready to be used for more complex analyses, so importing into qiime, trimming, and cleaning up the reads with dada2. Each step is more processing intensive than I expected and takes a lot of time (typing this while I wait on my dada2 denoising) so I think getting my reads prepared for visualizations and analysis is a good step.
